verdict.headline: Oil drops 4% on Iran diplomacy shift; chip stocks rebound broadly before Nvidia's print tomorrow
verdict.label: SPX 7,677 (+0.32%); Brent $88.58 (-4.9%); NVDA +2.47%; AMD +4.34%; DKS -31%; NVDA reports Wednesday AH
verdict.rationale_short: Brent's 4.9% drop to $88.58 is the session's defining move: Bessent's sanctions framework spared the institutions that clear Iran's oil money, and a Pakistani diplomat arrived in Tehran carrying a sanctions-relief proposal — the war premium is unwinding structurally. Both regime triggers are inactive (30Y at 5.23% vs. 5.30% threshold; Brent at $88.58 vs. $94 threshold). Chip stocks staged a broad recovery — NVDA +2.47% snapping a seven-session losing streak, AMD +4.34%, Intel +3.15%, Marvell +7% — but the recovery is pre-print positioning, not a fundamental signal. BTC hit an intraday high of $81,271 — its second consecutive breach of $80K — before settling at $78,313; the ceiling is real and has now been tested twice. DKS fell 31% on a guidance cut of 19% below consensus — consumer athletic spending is deteriorating. If NVDA delivers gross margin above 78% and a Q3 data-center guide above $39B simultaneously Wednesday AH, the chip-sector reset thesis is validated.

trade_setups.asset: NVDA (~$215) — 1 session to Wednesday AH print; de-risk cleared
trade_setups.thesis: NVDA enters the print having recovered from Monday's -2.9% drawdown: chip sector staged broad recovery Tuesday (AMD +4.34%, Intel +3.15%, Marvell +7%), Brent at $88.58 is no longer a macro headwind, and 30Y at 5.23% is 7bps from the trigger. The setup is materially more constructive than any comparable pre-print session this AI cycle. The execution bar is unchanged: consensus $92B revenue, $2.09 EPS. Dual gate required for a sustained rally: gross margin above 78% AND Q3 data-center guide materially above ~$39B simultaneously. NVDA has declined after 5 of the last 6 prints regardless of beat magnitude.
trade_setups.entry: Gross margin above 78% AND Q3 DC guide above $39B = the levels that define a constructive post-print tape. In-line on either leaves the multiple (~22x forward revenue) unchanged with sell-side at maximum consensus — the conditions for another altitude-ceiling reaction.
trade_setups.invalidation: Gross margin below 77% or Q3 DC guide below $37B. Either alone is a negative surprise at current multiple levels.

trade_setups.thesis: Two catalysts hit simultaneously Tuesday: Bessent's sanctions framework spared the institutions that actually clear Iran's oil money (removing the structural enforcement mechanism), and a Pakistani diplomat arrived in Tehran carrying a reported sanctions-relief proposal. Both together mark a shift from maximum-pressure enforcement toward a negotiating posture. The $94 regime trigger is now $5.42 away — the largest buffer since the trigger was established. If Pakistan-Iran talks produce a framework, Brent could test $85 or lower.
trade_setups.entry: Brent durably below $88 confirms the war premium is structurally unwound. Re-test above $92 would require a major escalation — Bessent announcing Chinese or Indian bank secondary sanctions, or an Iranian military action in the Strait.
trade_setups.invalidation: Pakistan-Iran talks collapse; Bessent's 'major financial institution announcement' targets Chinese crude buyers; Strait of Hormuz incident.
trade_setups.horizon: 3-5 sessions (Pakistan-Iran talks outcome; Bessent institution announcement pending)

trade_setups.asset: 30Y yield (5.23%) — Warsh keynote is the rate-path decision
trade_setups.thesis: The 30Y eased 1bp to 5.23% as Brent fell — oil/rate linkage holding. The 5.30% trigger is 7bps away, the largest buffer since it was set. Warsh's Friday keynote (Aug 28) is the decisive input: if he frames Canada tariff escalation and Iran energy dislocation as compounding inflation vectors, the 30Y could test 5.30% and restore the second regime indicator. A neutral-to-dovish keynote could push the 30Y back toward 5.10% and materially reduce the regime risk score. The Consumer Confidence Expectations Index at 68.2 (below 80 recession-risk threshold) gives him empirical support for either framing.
trade_setups.entry: 30Y above 5.30% = both regime indicators active simultaneously. 30Y below 5.10% = rate regime materially reduced for September FOMC.
trade_setups.invalidation: Warsh strikes unambiguously neutral-to-dovish tone; 30Y falls below 5.10%.
trade_setups.horizon: 4 sessions — Warsh keynote Friday Aug 28; September 16 FOMC is the medium-term context

bear_case: The day's constructive read rests on two assumptions: that the Pakistan-Iran diplomatic track is real and durable, and that NVDA delivers on both gross margin and the guide simultaneously. Both are low-probability as stated. Bessent called it 'Operation Economic Outcast' two days ago and has not signaled any pivot; the sanctions framework is still active and the war premium's decline is a sentiment trade, not a structural change. On NVDA: a beat without the guide has produced drawdowns five times in six attempts. AMD's ninth session below $484 means no structural reset has occurred — Tuesday's bounce is positioning, not confirmation. DKS's -31% on a 19%-below-consensus guidance cut is the consumer print that matters for the macro read: discretionary spending is deteriorating, and athletic wear is a leading indicator for broader consumer health. If NVDA disappoints Wednesday — the most likely single outcome based on base rates — the chip sector gives back Tuesday's recovery and Nasdaq tests 25,700-25,900. Add a hawkish Warsh Friday and the 30Y re-tests 5.30%, activating both regime indicators simultaneously for the first time. BTC's second rejection at $80K confirms the ceiling is structural; without NVDA follow-through and macro relief simultaneously, momentum fades toward the $75K-$76K support zone.
